title: Coordinate slip on one hidden grid: row digit from one letter, column digit from a letter s places on (8 grid shapes of 26-30 cells, slips -45..45, four role assignments, added constants; plus both lines slid)
k4_result: Idea as stated (one digit line at home, the other slid by s = -45..45, straight or crossed digits, every added constant on the straight lines, grids 2x13 13x2 3x9 9x3 4x7 7x4 5x6 6x5): 0 of 41,400 settings can be satisfied by ANY grid, with open ends and with wrapped ends. Hand reason for the straight roles: a cipher letter shares a row (or column) with its own plain letter, and the 24 clue pairs chain 21 letters into one class, so one row would need 21 cells (longest line available: 13); with a constant added, K = K at letter 74 and S = S at letter 33 force the constant back to 0. Extra (both lines slid, u, w = -45..45, u != w, straight and crossed, no constants): wrapped ends 0 of 128,160; open ends 308 of 128,160 survive, all on 4x7 / 7x4 / 5x6 / 6x5 and all with at least 36 of the 97 letters pushed off the end (at most 61 letters keep both digits), i.e. settings where one clue word is lost and little is tested. On those 308 no dictionary keyword grid fits (0 of 220,318 alphabets x 3-4 fills each), so there is no decryption to read. 0 undecided settings on K4. Separate finding: the cipher does not flatten English enough. Index of coincidence on 1,000 English 97-letter texts per shape: mean 0.048-0.054, 5th percentile 0.039-0.044; K4's 0.0361 is reached by 0.0-0.8% of messages depending on shape. And on grids with spare cells an English message usually lands on an empty cell: no empty cell in 100% (2x13), 18-22% (3x9, 9x3), 4% (4x7, 7x4), 0.5% (5x6, 6x5) of messages on random grids.
controls: 50 shuffled K4s, identical run. Idea as stated, open ends: 46 of 50 have 0 survivors, 4 have some (max 48 of 41,400); wrapped ends: 0 in all 50. K4's 0 is the usual result. Both lines slid, open ends: 134 to 1,110 survivors, median 364, mean 409 (K4 308; 33 of 50 controls at or above K4); wrapped ends 0 in all 50. Largest chained letter class on the home line: K4 21, controls 9-23, median 19. Dictionary grids on the survivors of 5 controls (224-1,112 settings each): 0 fits in all five, like K4. 51 control settings (of 17 million) hit the node limit and are counted as not surviving.
planted: 8/8: English 97-letter messages on dictionary keyword grids (5x6 slip 3; 3x9 slip 21; 6x5 by columns with the column line at home, slip -7; 4x7 slip 5 with constant 3; 2x13 slip -2 with constant 6; 5x6 both lines slid 2 and -4; crossed 5x6 slip 3; crossed 6x5 slip 11) all pass the any-grid test with open and wrapped ends, the planted keyword grid is found among 220,318 alphabets (1 fit in seven cases, 3 in one) and the text is read back 97/97. Solver check before the run: 194/194 random-grid encryptions feasible. Unit test: 6/6.
scope_limits: One grid, used for both writing digits and reading them back; 26 letters on 26-30 cells in the eight shapes listed (no 5x5 with a merged letter: K4 has all 26; no 6x6 with digits). One fixed slip for the whole message; slips up to 45 places. Constants only on the straight lines of the idea as stated (not when both lines are slid, not on crossed digits). Crossed digits tested as stated; on a grid that is not square they can only encipher letters whose digit exists on the other axis, which in practice means a 5x5 square with one letter set aside. Not covered: a slip that changes along the text or restarts in blocks (periodic bifid proper, where both digits of a cipher letter are row digits, is a different cipher and was not tested here), two different grids for writing and reading, digit lines permuted rather than slid, any transposition before or after. Open-end survivors of the both-lines-slid variant (slips of 34+ in both lines) are not excluded for a free grid; they are excluded only for dictionary keyword grids (220,318 alphabets on this machine, by rows or columns, spare cells first or last). The index-of-coincidence and empty-cell figures are for random grids and English taken from the K1-K3 plaintexts. Clue positions taken as exact.

negative.hypothesis: K4 was made by writing each plain letter as row and column digits in one hidden grid, sliding one line of digits s places along, and reading the digit columns back as letters, so each cipher letter has one coordinate from its own plain letter and one from a letter s places away.
negative.scope: Grids 2x13, 13x2, 3x9, 9x3, 4x7, 7x4, 5x6, 6x5 with ANY arrangement of the 26 letters (exact row/column placing test); one line at home and the other slid -45..45, straight and crossed digits, every added constant on straight lines (41,400 settings); plus both lines slid -45..45 without constants (128,160 settings); open and wrapped ends; dictionary keyword grids (220,318 alphabets, by rows / columns, spare cells first / last) on every survivor.
negative.outcome: Dead: 0 of 41,400 settings of the stated idea fit any grid (the clue pairs chain 21 letters into one row or column; K = K and S = S forbid a constant). Both lines slid: 0 of 128,160 with wrapped ends; 308 with open ends, all losing 36+ letters off the end, none with a dictionary grid. English under this cipher is also too rough: IC mean 0.048-0.054, K4's 0.036 reached by under 1% of messages (controls: 50 shuffled K4s give 0 survivors in 46 for the stated idea, 0 in all 50 wrapped, 134-1,110 open-end survivors for both lines slid against K4's 308; planted 8/8 found and read back 97/97).

follow_ups: Periodic bifid on the same 26-30 cell rectangles with a free grid: in each block of L letters the row digits are written first and then the column digits, so a cipher letter can take both digits from rows. The same placing solver decides it exactly for every L and block start once row digits and column digits share one value space; the old 6x6 bifid negative is only 'infeasible', and 5x5 is out for the 26 letters.
